bib.title: Unsupervised Data Augmentation for Consistency Training
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2020 (34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems); arXiv v6

question: Does replacing simple noise in semi-supervised consistency training with state-of-the-art data augmentation (RandAugment, back-translation) improve results with scarce labels?
hypothesis: Stronger data augmentations that work best in supervised learning also give superior performance when used to noise unlabeled examples in consistency training.
contributions: State-of-the-art supervised augmentations serve as superior noise in consistency training (Tables 1, 2)
UDA matches or beats supervised learning with orders of magnitude more labels (Table 4, Fig 4)
UDA combines with transfer learning (BERT) and is effective in high-data regimes (ImageNet)
Theoretical analysis of how UDA improves classification (Section 3)

method.summary: UDA minimises supervised cross-entropy on labeled data plus a consistency loss (KL/CE between predictions on an unlabeled example, from a fixed-parameter copy, and on its augmented version) weighted by lambda. Augmentations are RandAugment for images, back-translation (En-Fr, sampling) and TF-IDF word replacement for text. Extra techniques: confidence masking, sharpening, domain-relevance filtering, Training Signal Annealing.

datasets.name: IMDb
datasets.size: 25k labeled train; 20 labeled used in semi-sup

datasets.name: Yelp-2 / Yelp-5
datasets.source: Kaggle Yelp dataset; external unlabeled data (6m unlabeled for Yelp-5)

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.preprocessing: 100 augmented examples per unlabeled example generated before training

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.size: 10% labeled (rest unlabeled) or 100% labeled + 1.3M unlabeled from JFT

models.name: Random Transformer
models.architecture: BERT-base config with 6 hidden layers, 8 attention heads

models.name: BERT-base / BERT-large / BERT-finetune
models.init_from: BERT-base, BERT-large, or BERT-large further fine-tuned on in-domain unlabeled data

training.objective: CE(supervised) + lambda * CE(sharpened stop-grad p(y|x) || p(y|augmented x)), masked by confidence > beta; lambda=1 in most runs
training.optimizer: SGD with Nesterov momentum 0.9 (WRN-28-2); BERT optimizer not stated
training.lr: WRN: not stated; Shake-Shake/PyramidNet 0.03; ImageNet 10%: 0.3, full: 1.6; BERT finetune try 1e-5, 2e-5, 5e-5
training.lr_schedule: WRN: cosine decay cos(7t/(8T) * pi/2); Shake-Shake/PyramidNet: cosine, one annealing cycle; ImageNet: decayed by 10 four times
training.batch_size: WRN-28-2: 64 labeled / 448 unlabeled; Shake-Shake: 128 / 512; PyramidNet: 64 / 128; text with BERT: 32 / 224; ImageNet 10%: 512 / 15,360; ImageNet full: 8,192 / 16,384
training.steps: WRN-28-2 500K; Shake-Shake 300k; PyramidNet 700k; ImageNet 10% 40k; random Transformer 500k or 1M on Amazon-5/Yelp-5; BERT 30 to 100k tuned by data size
training.regularisation: EMA decay 0.9999 on WRN parameters; confidence masking beta 0.8 (CIFAR/SVHN), 0.5 (ImageNet); sharpening tau 0.4; TSA exp-schedule for low-label text; ImageNet 10% lambda=20, full set uses entropy minimisation
training.hardware: WRN-28-2: Tesla V100 GPU; text: v3-32 Cloud TPU Pod; Shake-Shake/PyramidNet: v3-32 TPU Pod; ImageNet 10%: v3-64; full: v3-128
training.seeds: 10 runs, mean and std for WRN-28-2 CIFAR/SVHN

other.bert_domain_finetune_grid: lr 2e-5/5e-5/1e-4, batch 32/64/128, steps 30k/100k/300k; chosen by BERT loss on held-out set
other.back_translation: WMT14 En-Fr models both directions, random sampling softmax temperature 0.7-0.9 best
other.randaugment: 15 transformations, magnitude in [1,10), probability fixed at 0.5, two ops per sub-policy
other.TSA: eta_t = alpha_t*(1-1/K)+1/K; alpha_t = 1-exp(-t/T*5) log, t/T linear, exp((t/T-1)*5) exp

inference.decoding: back-translation uses random sampling, temperature 0.7-0.9, not beam search
inference.samples: 1 augmented example per unlabeled example for BERT-finetune; 100 per unlabeled example precomputed for CIFAR-10

eval.protocol: CIFAR-10 and SVHN: mean and std over 10 runs; text and ImageNet: seed count not stated

limits: Five-category sentiment tasks still show a clear gap between UDA with 500 labels per class and BERT trained on the full supervised set
RandAugment magnitude range and probability not tuned; authors suggest tuning may help
Theory assumes in-domain, label-preserving, reversible augmentation (simplistic)
Dumped (offline) augmentations used for CIFAR-10; online augmentation said to be as good or better
Seed counts not stated for text and ImageNet; BERT optimizer and warmup not stated
Own MixMatch reimplementation slightly worse than reported, baselines in tables are reported by MixMatch

terms.definition: remove a labeled example from the loss when p(y*|x) exceeds a threshold eta_t that rises from 1/K to 1 over training
consistency loss computed only on examples whose max predicted probability exceeds beta

lineage.note: consistency training with adversarial noise; stop-gradient target taken from VAT

lineage.work: Oliver et al. realistic evaluation of SSL

figures.why: UDA beats VAT and MixMatch across label counts.
